---
title: "One dataset, two kinds of reference"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# chunks that fetch from NOAA run only when it is reachable
online <- requireNamespace("curl", quietly = TRUE) &&
  !is.null(curl::nslookup("www.ncei.noaa.gov", error = FALSE))
```

A virtual Icechunk repository keeps its metadata and coordinates itself
and points at the data where it already lives. Who can read what is
therefore decided in several places, at different times. This article
walks through them with a small real example: ten days of NOAA OISST v2.1
daily sea surface temperature (September 1981), from
[zarr-icechunk-assure](https://github.com/mdsumner/zarr-icechunk-assure).
The package ships the same repository built twice, once with references
into NOAA's `https://` archive and once into its `s3://` bucket.

```{r}
library(tabularberg)
https <- ic_example_oisst("https")
s3 <- ic_example_oisst("s3")
repo <- ic_repo_open(https$path)
repo
```

## What needs no credentials

Metadata, coordinates and history live in the repository, so they read
without authorising anything.

```{r}
ic_tags(repo)
ic_ancestry(repo, tag = "cf-repaired")[, c("snapshot_id", "message")]
```

The `as-virtualized` tag is the repository as first built, with a defect
kept on purpose: the `time` array has no `units` attribute. `cf-repaired`
adds them in a second commit. That commit touched metadata only; no
reference was rewritten.

```{r}
ic_diff(repo, from = list(tag = "as-virtualized"), to = list(tag = "cf-repaired"))
units <- function(tag) {
  meta <- ic_get(ic_session_readonly(repo, tag = tag), "time/zarr.json")
  jsonlite::fromJSON(rawToChar(meta))$attributes$units
}
units("as-virtualized")
units("cf-repaired")
```

## Where the bytes are

Each data chunk is a reference: a location, an offset and a length. The two
repositories hold the same byte ranges of the same files, named two ways.

```{r}
refs <- function(x) {
  s <- ic_session_readonly(ic_repo_open(x$path), tag = "cf-repaired")
  ic_chunk_refs(s, "/sst")[, c("key", "location", "offset", "length")]
}
r1 <- refs(https)
r2 <- refs(s3)
identical(r1[c("key", "offset", "length")], r2[c("key", "offset", "length")])
substr(c(r1$location[1], r2$location[1]), 1, 75)
```

Every reference falls under a *virtual chunk container*, a URL prefix the
repository declares along with how to reach it. A container is read only
once it is authorised, so an unauthorised read is refused before anything
is fetched:

```{r}
ic_repo_containers(repo)
s <- ic_session_readonly(repo, tag = "cf-repaired")
tryCatch(ic_get(s, "sst/c/0/0/0/0"), error = function(e) strwrap(conditionMessage(e), 75))
```

## Authorise and read

`ic_example_oisst()` returns the container prefix with a credential that
suits it: plain HTTP for the archive, anonymous access for the public
bucket. tabularberg returns chunk bytes; decoding them belongs to a Zarr
reader. These chunks are simple enough to decode in base R: zlib, then
undo a byte shuffle, then little-endian 16-bit integers.

```{r, eval = online}
chunk <- function(x) {
  s <- ic_session_readonly(ic_repo_open(x$path, authorize = x$authorize), tag = "cf-repaired")
  ic_get(s, "sst/c/0/0/0/0")
}
b1 <- chunk(https)
b2 <- chunk(s3)
identical(b1, b2)

unshuffle <- function(b, size) as.vector(t(matrix(b, nrow = length(b) %/% size, ncol = size)))
decode <- function(raw) {
  readBin(unshuffle(memDecompress(raw, "gzip"), 2L), "integer",
          n = 1440 * 720, size = 2, endian = "little")
}
p <- https$probe$probe
sst <- decode(b1)
sst[p$iy_stored * 1440 + p$ix + 1] * https$probe$array$scale_factor
```

That is 27.82 degrees C at longitude 199.875, latitude -9.875 on 1
September 1981, the probe value in the sample's `probe.json`.

## When each choice is made

zarr-icechunk-assure frames the choices by when they bind and whether they
can be undone:

- **Bake time: the reference flavour.** `https://...` or `s3://...` is
  written into every reference. Changing it means rewriting the references
  (for byterefs stores, `ic_byterefs_containers()` with a `target` remaps
  them as a repository is built). That is why the sample ships two
  repositories rather than one.
- **Deploy time: where the repository lives.** Here a zip unpacked to a
  temporary directory; the same repository could sit on S3, on a web
  server or in a zip read in place. The references never name it.
- **Open time: authorisation.** Which containers a session may read, with
  which credentials: `authorize` in `ic_repo_open()`. Authorising an S3
  container anonymously makes tabularberg read it with unsigned requests.
- **Read time: the tool.** The same location has dialects (`/vsis3/` in
  GDAL, `s3://` here, an `https://` endpoint), and the same credential may
  arrive as an environment variable for one reader and an argument for
  another.
- **Run time: where the reader runs.** Valid credentials can still be
  scoped by location; NASA Earthdata's direct S3 access, for example, works
  only from the same AWS region.

## Building the repository in R

The sample was built with icechunk-python from kerchunk-Parquet references
(assure's `py/make_repo.py`). The same build takes a page of R, from the
references and `probe.json` shipped with the package. Coordinates are
composed from the grid, not fetched; data arrays get metadata and
references only.

```{r}
dir <- system.file("extdata", "oisst-sample", package = "tabularberg")
P <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(dir, "probe.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
prefix <- P$cells$https$ref_prefix
shape <- unlist(P$array$shape)

zarr_json <- function(shape, chunks, dtype, fill, codecs, dims, attrs = list()) {
  charToRaw(jsonlite::toJSON(list(
    zarr_format = 3, node_type = "array", shape = as.list(shape), data_type = dtype,
    chunk_grid = list(name = "regular", configuration = list(chunk_shape = as.list(chunks))),
    chunk_key_encoding = list(name = "default", configuration = list(separator = "/")),
    fill_value = fill, codecs = codecs, attributes = attrs, dimension_names = as.list(dims)),
    auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = NA, always_decimal = TRUE))
}
bytes_le <- list(name = "bytes", configuration = list(endian = "little"))

built <- ic_repo_create(tempfile("oisst-built-"), containers = ic_container(prefix, "http"),
                        authorize = stats::setNames(list(ic_cred_http()), prefix))
w <- ic_session_writable(built, "main")
ic_set(w, "zarr.json", charToRaw('{"zarr_format":3,"node_type":"group","attributes":{}}'))

# coordinates, stored in the repository (uncompressed here)
ext <- unlist(P$grid$extent)
ny <- shape[3]
nx <- shape[4]
coords <- list(
  time = list(as.double(unlist(P$time$raw)), list(long_name = "Center time of the day")),
  zlev = list(0, list(units = "meters", positive = "down")),
  lat = list(ext[3] + (seq_len(ny) - 0.5) * (ext[4] - ext[3]) / ny, list(units = "degrees_north")),
  lon = list(ext[1] + (seq_len(nx) - 0.5) * (ext[2] - ext[1]) / nx, list(units = "degrees_east")))
for (nm in names(coords)) {
  v <- coords[[nm]][[1]]
  ic_set(w, paste0(nm, "/zarr.json"),
         zarr_json(length(v), length(v), "float64", 0, list(bytes_le), nm, coords[[nm]][[2]]))
  ic_set(w, paste0(nm, "/c/0"), writeBin(v, raw(), size = 8, endian = "little"))
}

# data arrays: metadata here, chunks as references into NOAA's files
codecs <- list(bytes_le,
               list(name = "numcodecs.shuffle", configuration = list(elementsize = 2L)),
               list(name = "numcodecs.zlib", configuration = list(level = 1L)))
attrs <- list(scale_factor = P$array$scale_factor, add_offset = P$array$add_offset,
              `_FillValue` = P$array$fill_value)
for (v in unlist(P$variables)) {
  ic_set(w, paste0(v, "/zarr.json"),
         zarr_json(shape, unlist(P$array$chunks), P$array$dtype, P$array$fill_value, codecs,
                   c("time", "zlev", "lat", "lon"), attrs))
  pq <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(file.path(dir, "refs-https", v, "refs.0.parq"))
  pq <- pq[!is.na(pq$path), ]   # padding rows are format, not data
  ic_set_virtual_refs(w, paste0("/", v), data.frame(
    dim_0 = seq_len(nrow(pq)) - 1L, dim_1 = 0L, dim_2 = 0L, dim_3 = 0L,
    location = pq$path, offset = pq$offset, length = pq$size))
}
ic_tag_create(built, "as-virtualized",
              ic_commit(w, "OISST 1981-09-01..10: virtual refs (units defect preserved)"))

# the repair, a metadata-only commit
w <- ic_session_writable(built, "main")
tm <- jsonlite::fromJSON(rawToChar(ic_get(w, "time/zarr.json")), simplifyVector = FALSE)
tm$attributes$units <- P$time$units_correct
tm$attributes$calendar <- P$time$calendar
ic_set(w, "time/zarr.json", charToRaw(jsonlite::toJSON(tm, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = NA)))
ic_tag_create(built, "cf-repaired", ic_commit(w, "Add CF time units (metadata-only repair)"))
```

The result matches the shipped repository: the same references and the
same array metadata for every data array, and the same repair between the
tags. (The coordinates differ only in compression: zarr-python stored them
with zstd.)

```{r}
ship <- ic_session_readonly(repo, tag = "cf-repaired")
mine <- ic_session_readonly(built, tag = "cf-repaired")
same <- function(v) {
  cols <- c("key", "location", "offset", "length")
  a <- ic_chunk_refs(ship, v)[, cols]
  b <- ic_chunk_refs(mine, v)[, cols]
  m <- function(s) jsonlite::fromJSON(rawToChar(ic_get(s, paste0(sub("^/", "", v), "/zarr.json"))))
  keep <- c("shape", "data_type", "codecs", "attributes", "dimension_names", "fill_value")
  c(refs = identical(a[order(a$key), ], b[order(b$key), ]),
    metadata = identical(m(ship)[keep], m(mine)[keep]))
}
sapply(c("/sst", "/anom", "/err", "/ice"), same)
ic_diff(built, from = list(tag = "as-virtualized"), to = list(tag = "cf-repaired"))
```

## Other readers

GDAL 3.14 has an Icechunk driver and reads these repositories' metadata and
coordinates, even from the zip in place
(`/vsiicechunk/{/vsizip/repo-https-2026-07-07.zip}/`). Its Zarr V3 support
does not yet decode `numcodecs.shuffle` and `numcodecs.zlib`
([GDAL issue 14917](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/issues/14917)), so the
data arrays wait on that.
